dm4.name: Search & other revenue growth
dm4.source: Alphabet quarterly results release / 10-Q, revenue by type (on results)
dm4.what: Growth in revenue from Google Search ads and related vs the same quarter last year.
dm4.why: About half of revenue and most of the profit; the first place AI-chatbot competition would show.
dm4.bull_means: Search ads still growing double digits despite AI chatbots.
dm4.neutral_means: Search growth slowing but still positive.
dm4.bear_means: Search is stalling: the core profit engine is under threat.

dm4.name: Google Cloud revenue growth
dm4.source: Alphabet quarterly results release / 10-Q, segment revenue (on results)
dm4.what: Growth in Google Cloud revenue vs the same quarter last year.
dm4.why: Cloud is where the $195-205bn of 2026 capital spending has to earn its return.
dm4.bull_means: AI demand is turning the spending into revenue fast.
dm4.neutral_means: Cloud still growing, but slower than the spending implies.
dm4.bear_means: Cloud growth back near 2025 levels while capex has doubled: spending is running ahead of demand.

dm5.name: Google worldwide search share (StatCounter)
dm5.source: StatCounter Global Stats, search engine market share, worldwide, monthly
dm5.what: Google's share of web searches worldwide from StatCounter, an independent web-traffic tracker, vs the same month a year earlier.
dm5.why: Monthly and independent, so it shows search losing ground before Alphabet reports. It does not count chatbot questions (see Known defects).
dm5.bull_means: Google is gaining share of searches.
dm5.neutral_means: Search share is steady (this does not prove chatbots aren't taking queries).
dm5.bear_means: Google is losing search share: a strong warning for the profit engine.

removed_indicators.reason: Alphabet gives no numeric next-quarter revenue or profit guidance (only capital-spending guidance), so guidance vs expectations can never be measured (Kenneth, 5 Oct 2026).

Trailing EPS is dominated by paper gains on the SpaceX and Anthropic stakes (gains added $2.35 to Q1 2026 and $6.26 to Q2 2026 diluted EPS), so trailing P/E vs its own history would read falsely cheap (Kenneth, 5 Oct 2026).

mix._note: Revenue mix (not scored). match = patterns on the row label printed in the SEC filing. groups = where Alphabet reports operating profit (segments).
mix.note: Alphabet reports operating profit for three segments only: Google Services (Search, YouTube ads, Network, Subscriptions), Google Cloud and Other Bets. So the four Services parts all show the Google Services margin. Hedging gains and losses are not a part (shown as Other when material). The 'whole company' margin in the mix table is the segment total before Alphabet's unallocated costs (e.g. part of AI research); Alphabet's reported operating margin is lower.
